Q1.q: Can groups from one country (dioceses, organisations, individual groups) register independently, or is approval or consolidated registration through the Bishops' Conference required?
Q1.a:
Each diocese, organisation or individual group in a country can register independently through the registration system; consolidated registration through the Bishops' Conference is not mandatory.
However, whether prior approval from the Bishops' Conference or national-level coordination is required may differ according to the internal policy of each Bishops' Conference, so please check with your Bishops' Conference or national WYD coordinator.

Q2.q: How many leaders and deputy leaders are required for each group size, and can additional leaders be appointed later? Also, what information can group leaders and subgroup leaders view and manage?
Q2.a:
A Single Group and a Macrogroup each consist of one group leader and one deputy leader. If the group is large, or if members have different arrival/departure dates in Seoul or different packages, Subgroups can be formed within the Macrogroup. A Subgroup can be created with an account separate from the Macrogroup leader's account, in which case one leader and one deputy leader are also appointed for the Subgroup.
The Subgroup leader and deputy leader can view and edit the Subgroup's registration information and make payments. For Subgroups created with a separate account, the Macrogroup leader can view the registration information and make payments, but is not given permission to edit the information directly.

Q3.q:
Can one family be recognised as a single Subgroup within a Macrogroup? What is the minimum number of people?
Also, when minors are separated from adults in shared accommodation, who is responsible for them?
Q3.a:
There is no minimum number of people for a Macrogroup. The criteria for forming a Subgroup within a Macrogroup are the same package and the same arrival/departure dates in Seoul. Therefore, if a family chooses the same package and stays in Seoul on the same dates, they can form one Subgroup.
According to the WYD Seoul Safeguarding Guidelines for minors, the basic principle is that adults and minors are accommodated separately. However, this needs to be applied together with the safeguarding regulations of each country's Bishops' Conference and national rules, as well as practical safety requirements.
For example, some countries stipulate that even adult chaperones may not share accommodation with minors. In such cases, chaperones can stay in a space close to the minors' accommodation so that they can respond quickly if a problem arises. In other countries, two adult chaperones stay in the minors' accommodation and take turns supervising.
Conversely, if a country's Bishops' Conference or national standards judge it more appropriate, for the safety and protection of minors, for adult chaperones to stay in the same space as the minors in their care, they may also stay in the same space in accordance with those standards. Even in this case, appropriate protective measures must be in place, such as appointing a minor representative who can contact the chaperone immediately in an emergency.
Therefore, various approaches may be applied to accommodation for minors depending on each country's safeguarding regulations and the safety situation on site, and it is difficult to set a single policy that applies uniformly to every case.
The WYD Seoul Local Organising Committee presents the WYD Seoul Safeguarding Guidelines for minors while respecting the safeguarding guidelines and standards of each country's Bishops' Conference, which are co-LOCs. However, the decision on which accommodation arrangement to choose under those standards, and the responsibility that follows, rests with each pilgrim group.

Q4.q: If a representative registered under our diocese (vicariate) is coming from another country (e.g. the child of a parishioner living abroad who wishes to accompany their parents), is it correct to register them under our organisation?
Q4.a: Even participants who live abroad or depart from another country can be included and registered in your group if they will take part as members of your diocesan (vicariate) group and act under the guidance and supervision of the group leader. For example, the child of a parishioner living abroad who joins your diocesan group together with their parents can also be registered in the same group.

Q5.q: For international organisations or bodies made up of several countries or dioceses, how should registration and package selection be done when members of the same group or Macrogroup arrive or depart on different dates, at different times, on different flights or by different means of transport?
Q5.a: Register one Macrogroup under the name of your international organisation or diocese, then form and register Subgroups of participants who share the same package and the same stay dates in Seoul. Each Subgroup can register up to 150 people.

Q6.q: Do priests, deacons and religious register as members of a regular pilgrim group, or do they need to register separately? Is the same method used when a priest belongs to a Macrogroup?
Q6.a: Priests, deacons and religious all register as participants in a regular pilgrim group. In the case of a Macrogroup, the actual registration of pilgrims is done by Subgroup, so they register as part of the Subgroup they belong to. Unlike regular pilgrims, priests and deacons must have their personal information entered separately for identity verification and clergy-related preparations, and the group leader collects this information and enters it into the registration system.

Q7.q: We are coordinators of an international group. Is it better to create one Macrogroup with Subgroups by country, or to create a separate Macrogroup for each country with Subgroups by package within it?
Q7.a: It is best to choose the registration structure of an international group by considering how the group operates and the role of each national coordinator. If the international coordinator manages the whole group and national coordinators manage each Subgroup, you may consider forming national Subgroups under one Macrogroup. On the other hand, if each country manages its participants and handles registration and payment independently, forming a separate Macrogroup for each country may be more convenient. Please consider whether to form Subgroups by package according to each country's participant composition and package choices.

Q8.q: If the number of pilgrims in a Single Group increases, is it automatically converted into a Macrogroup?
Q8.a: Even if the number of pilgrims in a Single Group increases, it is not automatically converted into a Macrogroup. A Single Group can register up to 150 people, so if the number of participants may exceed 150, you should register as a Macrogroup from the start. The group type is chosen when registration begins and cannot be changed once registration has started.

Q9.q: You said the difference between a Single Group and a Macrogroup is not simply the number of people. What conditions (characteristics) must be met to become a Macrogroup, and what are the advantages of registering as a Macrogroup?
Q9.a: The difference between a Single Group and a Macrogroup lies not only in the number of participants but also in the participation schedule, package composition and the way registration is managed. A Single Group registers up to 150 people as one group without separate Subgroups and is suitable when all participants have the same schedule and package. A Macrogroup can register up to 5,000 people and can manage participants with different schedules or packages by dividing them into Subgroups. Each Subgroup is made up of participants with the same package and the same arrival and departure dates. The advantage of a Macrogroup is that it can have several Subgroups under one organisation while each Subgroup handles registration, information changes and payment independently. Therefore, please choose the registration method by considering not only the size of the group but also the variety of schedules and packages and the need to manage each Subgroup separately.

Q10.q: Do people who belong to the same group but travel to Korea individually need to form a separate Subgroup?
Q10.a: Even if they travel to Korea individually, if they will follow the same schedule during the event, use the same package and act under the guidance and supervision of the same group leader, they can be registered in the same group without forming a separate Subgroup. However, if participants choose different packages or have different participation schedules, a Subgroup may be needed, so please check the detailed criteria in the registration system.

Q11.q: We are a Single Group of fewer than 150 people arriving by two different means of transport. Can we register as the same group and be picked up at two different places?
Q11.a:
Even if a Single Group of fewer than 150 people arrives by different means of transport, it can be registered as the same group if it will participate with the same schedule and package under the guidance and supervision of the same group leader.
However, registering as the same group and being picked up at two different places are separate matters. The Local Organising Committee currently has no plans to provide a pick-up service on arrival at the airport, so please travel on your own from each arrival point to the check-in location and your accommodation. When travelling from your accommodation to the main event venues and catechesis locations, you can use public transport with the transport card included in your package.

Q12.q: Is there a limit on the number of Macrogroups that can be formed per diocese?
Q12.a: There is no limit on the number of Macrogroups; only the number of people within a group is limited to 5,000 or fewer.

Q13.q: What role does the Bishops' Conference play in the registration process? Must every group be approved by the youth department of the Bishops' Conference?
Q13.a: Each Bishops' Conference can decide its own role in the registration process. The LOC does not require all groups from a country to obtain approval from the youth department of their Bishops' Conference in order to register.

Q14.q: Our group will take part in the Days in the Dioceses but will prepare its own programme (and arrange its own accommodation) and does not need logistical support from the LOC. Should we tick 'Yes' or 'No' for participation in the Days in the Dioceses on the registration portal?
Q14.a: Please tick 'Yes' for participation, for reference in preparing and running the Days in the Dioceses.

Q15.q: From the start of registration, will direct support be provided so that national coordinators can resolve registration enquiries? Will a complete video with step-by-step guidance also be provided?
Q15.a: We are preparing support measures and guidance materials so that national coordinators can respond smoothly to registration enquiries. Direct support for coordinators and whether to provide a complete video explaining the registration procedure step by step are currently being reviewed and discussed internally, and we will announce the details and schedule as soon as they are confirmed.

Q16.q: Is a group registration officially confirmed (including allocation of zones, accommodation, etc.) only after full payment, or is it already confirmed when basic information is first submitted on the registration portal?
Q16.a: A group registration is officially confirmed only after the participation contribution has been paid in full.

Q17.q: What documents are required for the registration and verification of priests? Are a Celebret, a faculty to minister and a certificate of good standing required? Also, for priests belonging to a religious institute, is a certificate from the provincial superior sufficient, or is a certificate from the diocesan bishop required?
Q17.a: Priests register as members of their group. For verification of priestly status, they must submit a photo of their ID, a certificate of priestly status issued by the competent authority of their diocese, and a confirmation of the protection of minors and vulnerable adults. Priests belonging to a religious institute may submit a certificate from their provincial superior.

Q18.q: When does registration start? Can the registration of pilgrims in a Macrogroup be done in stages, or must it be completed all at once?
Q18.a: Online registration is scheduled to open on 23 October, and you do not need to complete the entire registration of a Macrogroup at once. You can use the 'Save as draft' function in the registration system to save what you have entered and then add information or edit it later. Please proceed with payment after entering and checking all the required registration information. You can also form Subgroups within the Macrogroup, register the Subgroups that are ready first, and register the remaining groups one by one as they become ready.

Q19.q: What are the age criteria and participation limits for pilgrims, and in what capacity should young people over 30 and adults in their 40s and 50s or older companions register?
Q19.a: WYD is an event designed mainly for young people aged 14 to 30, but it is open to everyone who wishes to take part, and there are no separate limits on the age or number of pilgrims. Therefore, participants over 30, adults in their 40s and 50s, and older companions can all register as members of a pilgrim group without any separate category.

Q20.q: Can participants be added or removed, or entered information be edited, during the registration process?
Q20.a: Yes. Before payment is completed, the group leader can increase or decrease the total number of participants in the registration system and can also edit the information entered for priests and deacons, pilgrims with disabilities and visa applicants. After payment is completed, please contact the Local Organising Committee to request changes. Please note, however, that even if the number of participants decreases, the participation contribution for those people will not be refunded.

Q21.q: If someone cancels, can their place be transferred to someone on a waiting list or to another pilgrim, and when and to what extent can changes be made?
Q21.a: Pilgrims other than the group leader and deputy leader can be replaced by another participant regardless of when they registered or whether payment has been made. Therefore, you can replace a pilgrim who cancels with someone on a waiting list or another pilgrim. Please note, however, that if the total number of participants in the group decreases after payment because a participant is not replaced, the amount paid for the reduced number will not be refunded.

Q22.q: If a leader enters a pilgrim's information incorrectly, can the pilgrim correct it themselves?
Q22.a: Pilgrims cannot edit their own information directly in the registration system. Individual participant information needs to be entered only for the group leader and deputy leader, priests and deacons, pilgrims with disabilities and participants who need visa support. If the group leader enters such information incorrectly, the group leader can correct it directly before payment is completed. If changes are needed after payment is completed, please send a request to the Local Organising Committee (inquiries@wydseoul.org).

Q23.q: If we are unable to attend WYD for unavoidable reasons, is a refund possible at any stage, or is there no refund at all once all payment stages are completed? (e.g. war, natural disasters)
Q23.a: In principle, the participation contribution is not refundable. As an exception, a refund is given only when a visa application has been refused and supporting documents confirming this are submitted. Refunds are processed after the event, and the amount paid out excludes related fees. At present, reasons other than visa refusal, such as war or natural disasters, are not included as grounds for a refund, but we will consider these reasons carefully as well.

Q24.q: Can we receive an official invoice or a bill with an official seal for international remittance and accounting purposes?
Q24.a: At present, no standardised invoice is issued. However, we understand that legal and accounting requirements for international remittances differ by country and organisation, and the LOC is reviewing in what form it can provide the documents needed for payment, on the basis of payment made directly to the LOC. We will let you know the outcome as soon as it is confirmed.

Q25.q: Within the same Macrogroup, can each Subgroup choose a different package and pay separately? We would also like to know how a payment delay by some Subgroups affects the whole Macrogroup.
Q25.a: Yes, within the same Macrogroup each Subgroup can choose a different package and pay separately. Please form each Subgroup with pilgrims who will use the same stay dates in Seoul and the same package for the main event. Since payment is made by Subgroup, even if payment by some Subgroups is delayed, it does not affect the registration and payment of other Subgroups or the Macrogroup.

Q26.q: What are the payment schedules and deadlines for registration and each package? Can we be informed of the deadline for each item, such as the first payment, instalments, the balance and insurance?
Q26.a:
Payment is possible from the day the registration system opens. The payment deadlines depend on the package type and payment method, as follows.
- Packages with accommodation: by 31 May 2027
- Packages without accommodation: before on-site registration opens (on-site registration opens in late July; the exact date will be announced later)
- Packages without accommodation (international bank transfer): by 30 June 2027
Because international bank transfers take time between banks, the deadline is earlier even for packages without accommodation. If you are unable to complete payment by the deadline, you can pay through on-site registration (on-site registration opens in late July; the exact date will be announced later).
When paying in instalments, there is no separate deadline for the first payment. However, the full amount must be paid by the deadlines above. The Participation Contribution cannot be split by package item and can only be paid as the full package amount.

Q27.q: How much is the participation fee, and by what methods and in what currencies can it be paid? Is it only possible in dollars, or can it also be paid in euros? What is included in 'other payment methods', and can different organisations split the payment for one group?
Q27.a:
The participation fee can be found on the official website. Payment is made in Korean won in the Republic of Korea and in US dollars in other countries. If you select 'pay in local currency' on the payment screen, you can also pay in the currencies of major countries, and any additional fees incurred are borne by the payer. The payment methods are as follows.
-Credit card / debit card
-Bank transfer (virtual account)
-Simple payment: Naver Pay and Kakao Pay in Korea; Apple Pay and Alipay abroad

Q28.q: Are the Participation Contribution and the Solidarity Fund mandatory? According to survey results, many groups need financial support yet have to pay in addition to the registration fee, so we wonder whether the Participation Contribution is really mandatory. We would also like to know whether the Solidarity Fund can be designated to support pilgrims from a particular country or region.
Q28.a:
Taking part in World Youth Day itself is free of charge. However, to participate as a 'registered participant', you must pay the Participation Contribution. Registered participants who have paid the contribution choose the package they want and receive accommodation, meals, transport, insurance and a pilgrim kit. Those who take part without registering do not receive these packages.
The Solidarity Fund is a voluntary donation that helps more pilgrims to take part, especially young people from countries in difficult circumstances. Payment is not mandatory; the fund is made up of voluntary contributions from pilgrims who share its purpose.

Q29.q: How much does registration and participation cost for each package, and are there discounts depending on Macrogroup size or for early or lump-sum payment? We would also like to know whether minors pay the same fee as adults and whether there are separate discounts or financial support.
Q29.a: The Participation Contribution for each package can be found on the official website and applies equally to all pilgrims regardless of age. There are no discounts for minors, group size, early payment, etc. Instead, the Local Organising Committee has tried to set the Participation Contribution for each package at the lowest reasonable level so that all pilgrims can take part.

Q30.q: What are the eligibility requirements for countries, groups and individual pilgrims to receive support from the Solidarity Fund, and through what procedure and channel (Local Organising Committee, DLFL, website, email, etc.) is the application made? Is it possible for only some pilgrims, rather than the whole Macrogroup, to apply for support?
Q30.a: The LOC is currently reviewing the eligibility requirements and application procedure for the Solidarity Fund in consultation with the Dicastery for Laity, Family and Life. Details such as eligibility requirements and how to apply will be announced as soon as they are confirmed.

Q31.q: Will representatives of Bishops' Conferences also be given a management function to access the 'back office' of the online registration system and check the groups and group leaders registered from their country? This has been possible at every WYD over the past ten years.
Q31.a: Representatives of Bishops' Conferences can request access to view the registration system back office (read-only) from the DLFL. This allows them to check the registration status of their country.

Q32.q: Please let us know whether there is a separate registration procedure for bishops and for their participation in catechesis. Please also explain the check-in procedure according to the type of accommodation for bishops and the collection of items for clergy.
Q32.a: Bishops also register through the registration system (bishops). Bishops who will lead catechesis will be selected and managed by the DLFL. Bishops staying in hotels designated by the Local Organising Committee will check in at those hotels, and they can also collect their items at the hotel. Check-in and item collection for bishops using other accommodation are currently under discussion.

Q33.q: Can bishops choose between a homestay and a hotel? If they can choose a homestay, why are bishops given this option rather than giving priority to young pilgrims? Also, does the LOC cover the cost of the hotels offered to bishops, and what type of room (single room, etc.) is provided?
Q33.a: Bishops can choose between a hotel, a homestay, staying with the group they accompany, or arranging their own accommodation. This is to allow bishops to choose according to their circumstances. Bishops pay for hotel accommodation themselves. A single room will be allocated as standard.

Q34.q: Which countries are subject to and exempt from K-ETA in 2027, and can it be applied for individually or as a group?
Q34.a:
Currently, until 31 December 2026, K-ETA applies to 88 countries and 22 countries are exempt from K-ETA. For details, please refer to
https://www.k-eta.go.kr/portal/board/viewboarddetail.do?bbsSn=299706&esntlPnotiMtYn=Y to check whether your country is exempt. We are discussing with the Ministry of Justice whether the K-ETA exemption can be extended to next year.
Also, K-ETA cannot be applied for as a group; please apply individually.

Q35.q: Will the LOC provide the address of the place of stay in Korea and the contact details required for visa applications?
Q35.a: For the address of your place of stay in Korea and your contact details when applying for a visa, you may enter the Local Organising Committee's information. This information can be found in the confirmation of participation issued by the registration system.

Q36.q: Our group has pilgrims of various nationalities. Will guidance materials be provided to check whether a visa or K-ETA is needed for each nationality? We would also like to know whether there is a dedicated WYD visa, the nature of the C-3 visa, and whether visa-exempt participants need a letter of invitation.
Q36.a: The Local Organising Committee does not provide separate visa guidance materials. Since visa and K-ETA requirements differ by nationality, please visit https://www.visa.go.kr/ to check the visa requirements for each country. There is no dedicated WYD visa. The C-3 is a short-term stay visa; detailed information on the length of stay is being discussed with the government and will be announced later. Visa-exempt participants do not need a letter of invitation.

Q37.q: Are the Local Organising Committee or the DLFL informing Korean embassies and consulates in each country about WYD and the visa procedures for participants? Will support with visa appointments, group applications, arrangements for pilgrims living far from an embassy (e.g. batch applications) and special consideration for the purpose of attending WYD be provided?
Q37.a: The Local Organising Committee is informing and communicating with Korean embassies and consulates about the WYD visa procedures. For this 2nd International Preparatory Meeting as well, we received a great deal of help through consultation with the government. The LOC will continue to work with the Korean government to simplify visa procedures and will provide information later.

Q38.q: How much is the visa fee, and are fee waivers or discounts for pilgrims attending WYD being considered?
Q38.a: The visa fee and whether fee waivers or discounts will be offered to WYD participants are currently being discussed with the relevant authorities. We will let you know as soon as this is confirmed.

Q39.q: Is there support for alternative documents that can be used by pilgrims who find it difficult to submit a certificate of employment or pay slips, such as students?
Q39.a: We are currently consulting with the relevant authorities on the visa documents required for students, young participants and others. We will announce the specific submission requirements, including alternative documents, as soon as they are confirmed.

Q40.q: What does it cost to take part as an international volunteer, and can visa holders apply for long-term volunteering?
Q40.a:
There is no participation fee for international long-term volunteers. The Local Organising Committee provides accommodation, lunch vouchers on weekdays, and part of the transport and meal costs; other costs must be borne by the volunteer.
International volunteers must obtain a visa to serve in Korea for a long period (three months or more), and most receive a religious visa (D-6). Those who already hold a visa can also apply, which has the advantage of making entry much easier. Please note, however, that even if you hold a visa, you must go through the same application procedure for international long-term volunteers and may likewise be asked to submit a letter of recommendation from your diocese or Bishops' Conference.

Q41.q: What are the procedures and preparations for consultation and collaboration with the volunteer committee?
Q41.a: A volunteer section will be set up on the official website in the future. Until then, please contact volunteer.intl@wydseoul.org.

Q42.q: What is the difference between long-term and short-term volunteers, and what are the eligibility requirements and registration procedures?
Q42.a:
1. Long-term volunteering
Long-term volunteers serve at the Local Organising Committee for three months or more and take part in preparing and planning WYD Seoul 2027. They are divided into department volunteers and team volunteers depending on their hours and area of work, and recruitment (separate for those living in Korea and abroad) is announced on the Local Organising Committee website. Those selected from abroad as long-term volunteers are provided with accommodation as well as part of their meal and transport costs.
2. Short-term volunteering
Short-term volunteers serve mainly during the main event from 3 to 8 August 2027. As at previous events, their service begins about a week before the main event, so they must enter Korea by 26 July and take part from the preparatory programmes, such as training and the volunteers' sending Mass. Applications for short-term volunteering will be made through the official volunteer registration system.

Q43.q: How many seats do buses commonly used for group travel in Korea have? What is the availability and supply of 45-seat and 53-seat buses?
Q43.a: Group buses commonly used in Korea are only 45-seaters. The event takes place during the holiday season, so the supply of buses is not a problem, but costs may be higher than usual.

Q44.q: What are the operating hours of public transport such as the subway and buses during WYD? Are there plans for late-night or 24-hour service, extended hours, or additional services to cope with congestion during the event? Also, what transport measures will be in place for travel between accommodation and the main event venues?
Q44.a: To make public transport convenient for pilgrims during WYD, we are in ongoing discussions with the Seoul Metropolitan Government and relevant agencies about increasing subway, bus and other public transport services.

Q45.q: Can you confirm whether members of the same group may arrive in and depart from Seoul on different flights, even if their arrival and departure dates are the same?
Q45.a: Participants in the same group may arrive in and depart from Seoul on different flights. If their arrival and departure dates are the same, they use the same package and they participate under the guidance and supervision of the same group leader, there is no need to form a separate Subgroup simply because their flights differ.

Q46.q: Can married couples or families request to stay in the same accommodation?
Q46.a:
If married couples or families wish to stay together, please register them in the same group. As a rule, participants in the same group are allocated to the same accommodation.
However, since allocation is based on the overall capacity and operating criteria of the accommodation, we ask for your understanding that individual accommodation requests are difficult to accommodate. Even if you are allocated to the same accommodation, a family room or sharing the same room is not guaranteed.

Q47.q: What type of accommodation is provided in the pilgrim package, and what items, such as sleeping bags, should participants bring themselves? Also, how will additional accommodation be secured if the expected number of participants is exceeded?
Q47.a:
The accommodation included in the packages is provided as shared accommodation in parishes, schools, public facilities, etc., and as homestays.
Bedding is not provided, so participants should bring their own sleeping bag or other personal bedding. The Local Organising Committee is working to secure a certain amount of reserve accommodation in case the expected number of participants is exceeded.
However, please understand that it will be difficult for the LOC to provide accommodation for additional participants after the deadline for packages with accommodation (31 May 2027).

Q48.q: If a group arranges its own accommodation, such as a hotel, should it inform the Local Organising Committee of the accommodation details?
Q48.a:
During registration, there is a field for entering the details of accommodation you have arranged yourselves.
However, this information is requested for reference only and is not mandatory.

Q49.q: Can group leaders visit or check the allocated accommodation in advance before WYD? Also, if the actual accommodation differs from the facilities and conditions announced in advance, can a change of accommodation be requested, and what is the procedure?
Q49.a: Even if accommodation is allocated before the event, visiting may be difficult if it is a public facility. However, you can check the location of the parish where you will check in and of your allocated accommodation. Judging from past events, there are so many variables with accommodation that we recommend keeping in mind the various situations that may arise even after allocation. You can request a change of accommodation, but the change procedure will go ahead only if necessary after the reason has been reviewed.

Q50.q: Will accommodation be allocated within Seoul, or can it also be allocated outside Seoul? How is access to the main WYD venues and public transport taken into account, and when and how will each group be informed of the location of its allocated accommodation and responsible parish?
Q50.a:
Most accommodation will be within Seoul. However, in some cases accommodation may be located on the outskirts. Even on the outskirts, we plan to choose places from which Seoul can be reached by public transport.
Allocation results will be sent out in stages by email from about one month before the event.
